body.html: Triple B Boutique Residence overview — who it suits — to put it as simply as possible, Triple B Boutique Residence is a residence-style stay for anyone who wants "a clean room, a comfy bed, and a central Si Racha location" on a very light budget · it isn't a beachfront resort that lets you walk straight down to the water, and it isn't a luxury chain hotel with a grand lobby · it's a compact boutique stay of around 47 rooms in Surasak, Si Racha — a neighbourhood that mixes people working in the industrial estates, Japanese families on assignment, and travellers stopping over before heading on to Pattaya or Rayong · the building sits in the middle of town near the shops and restaurants, so the selling point is convenience and value rather than luxury · real reviews line up on who fits best here: people coming to work in the eastern industrial zone for a few nights, travellers who want a clean, low-cost room in town, couples or groups of friends using Si Racha as a base for day trips to Pattaya, and people looking for a monthly stay close to work · another group that calls it worthwhile is anyone who doesn't need a full set of facilities but just wants a good room, a good bed, and an easy walk to the mall · if you're after a quiet, luxurious beachfront resort with a spa, several restaurants, and five-star service, this may not be the answer — look toward Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · in short, it's a place that "does the basics well" at a price that's hard to match in the same area

Location and getting around — Triple B's strong point is that it sits in central Si Racha, on the Surasak side, which makes both the town centre and the main routes easy to reach · from the property you can walk to Robinson Si Racha and Pacific Park in just a short stretch (about 400 metres, or under a 10-min walk), the town's main shopping centre with restaurants, supermarkets, and a cinema · many reviewers praise the location as "easy to walk anywhere," with convenience stores, restaurants, ramen shops, and cafés all around, so you don't need a car for every meal · it's near the Sriracha Shinto Shrine and Si Racha Junction railway station, both within easy reach · for those working, the property is an easy drive to the Laem Chabang industrial estates and port and the industrial zones in this area · importantly, it's only about a 20-min drive from Pattaya and roughly an hour from both Suvarnabhumi and U-Tapao airports, which makes it a handy base for both work and travel · if you want to drop by nearby attractions, Khao Kheow Open Zoo, Sriracha Tiger Zoo, or Ko Loy Si Racha are all a short drive away · one small note: Si Racha is an industrial town where traffic gets fairly heavy at rush hour, and the town centre is lively with some traffic noise, so if you have to head to Laem Chabang in the morning allow extra time, and if you're a light sleeper choose a room that doesn't face the main road

"Super clean room, the bed was soft and comfier than the price suggests, and the bathroom was big · just a few minutes' walk to Robinson, with restaurants and convenience stores all around. I came to work near Laem Chabang and staying here was convenient and great value."

Room types and decor — Triple B has around 47 rooms split into several types to suit your group size and budget · it starts with the Standard Room, a standard room for a solo traveller or a couple on a budget · stepping up are the Deluxe Double Room with balcony (one large bed) and the Deluxe Twin Room with balcony (two single beds), which suit friends or co-workers travelling together · the largest is the Deluxe Studio, which has both a double and a single bed in one room, good for a small family or a group of three · something many rooms have is a private balcony, which makes the room feel airy and lets in natural light · the decor is a warm, contemporary boutique style — simple but clean-looking · in-room amenities cover the basics for a regular stay, with a flat-screen TV (many reviews say it has Netflix), air conditioning, fridge, kettle, tea and coffee, hairdryer, work desk, and free drinking water · what real reviews praise most consistently is that the rooms are clean, the beds are very comfortable, the bathrooms are large and clean, and the rooms are bigger than expected for the price · the strong air conditioning is another point that draws praise · for anyone working or taking online meetings, the work desk and free Wi-Fi do the job well · one thing worth knowing: because it's a small residence-style stay, the decor leans toward being plain and practical rather than luxurious, and some details may not be as polished as a big chain hotel — which is fair for the price

Facilities, pool, and gym — for a stay this size, Triple B gives you fairly good value on facilities · the highlight is the rooftop pool with sun terrace, a spot to head up to for the breeze and a photo of the town view in the evening · to be honest, in line with real reviews, the pool is on the small side — it's a pool for cooling off and lounging rather than serious laps, so if you're hoping for a long pool, adjust your expectations · there's also a gym for anyone who wants to work out during their stay, and some reviews say the equipment is decent · on the basics, it has it all: 24-hour front desk, 24-hour check-in, 24-hour security, daily housekeeping, free parking, and free Wi-Fi in all rooms · there's a lift, and a convenience store in the building makes it easy to grab food and supplies · what puts long-stay guests at ease is being able to check in around the clock, which suits shift workers or anyone arriving late · overall the facilities here aren't resort-level in number, but they're "just right and genuinely usable" for an in-town stay, plus a rooftop pool and gym that aren't easy to find at the same price

Food and bar — on food, set your expectations straight first: Triple B is a residence-style stay, so it doesn't have a large restaurant or bar like a chain hotel · there is breakfast on offer, which from real reviews is clearly a point people see differently — those who like it say breakfast is fine for the price, especially Thai dishes like rice porridge with side dishes that many find tasty · while those who don't feel the Western options are limited, and some reviews complain that dishes like eggs sometimes aren't served as hot as they should be · the takeaway is that breakfast is a passable add-on, not a reason to come here in the first place · the upside is the location helps a lot, because the property is in the middle of town and you can easily walk to Robinson Si Racha and the restaurants all around — nearby there are Thai restaurants, ramen and Japanese spots (fitting the Japanese community in Si Racha), grilled-meat places, cafés, and convenience stores, so many people choose to eat out mainly · for long-stay guests who want to cook a bit themselves, being close to the mall and market makes buying ingredients easy · overall food isn't Triple B's selling point, but sitting amid Si Racha's good eateries makes up for it nicely

Service — service is a point that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews, which is a strength for a small stay like this · those who were impressed say the staff are friendly, cheerful, kind, and helpful · some foreign reviews note that a few front-desk staff speak English well, which makes communication easy for foreigners working in this area · the overall feel is the relaxed warmth of a small place that can look after guests thoroughly, and having a 24-hour front desk is reassuring when you arrive late or have something to ask · to be straight about it, because it's a small team, some services may not be as formal or as fast as a big chain hotel at busy times, but in terms of care and friendliness it does well, and that's one reason the review scores come out good · a tip: if you have a special request — a high-floor room, a room not facing the road, or an early check-in — let them know in advance and confirm again before you travel

Voices from real reviews (both praise and criticism) — pulling from Trip.com, Agoda, and TripAdvisor, the picture leans fairly positive, especially on platforms with a large number of reviews · on the praise side: rooms that are very clean and bigger than the price, beds that are especially comfortable, big clean bathrooms, strong air conditioning, a large TV with Netflix, a central location within walking distance of Robinson and restaurants all around, friendly staff who speak English, free parking, and a rooftop pool and gym that aren't easy to find at this price · many sum it up as "more than worth the price" and a place they come back to when they have business around Si Racha and Laem Chabang · on the watch-out side: what comes up is the small pool, better for a soak than a swim, breakfast with few Western options and some meals not served hot, a location in an industrial town with traffic noise and occasionally some smell from the area, and limited English TV channels · on TripAdvisor, where the sample is small, the score looks lower than other platforms because some negative reviews are mixed in, while Trip.com, with a large number of reviews, gives it a high-8 score · most of these criticisms are about setting expectations to match "a low-cost boutique stay in the town centre" rather than being big problems that keep people from returning

"I've stayed several times now when I come to work around here — clean room, soft bed every time, lovely staff who speak English · the only downsides are the pool's a bit small and there's not much choice for a Western breakfast, but for this price it's great value. I'll definitely be back next time."

Price comparison and value — Triple B's starting price is around ฿800/night at normal rates (during some promotional periods it can drop to roughly ฿600–700 depending on room type and dates, equivalent to about 23 dollars), and the larger deluxe or studio rooms move up to roughly ฿900–1,000+ by size and season · what makes it especially worthwhile for long-stay guests is a monthly rate starting around ฿7,000 a month, which is great value for anyone working in the industrial zone for a long stretch · compared with other stays in Si Racha town and the Laem Chabang area, Triple B feels very good value in terms of room quality for the price, because you get a clean room, a good bed, a large bathroom, plus a rooftop pool, gym, and free parking, on a budget cheaper than many high-rise hotels in the same area · if you plan to use Si Racha as a base for work in the industrial zone, a short stopover on a trip, or day trips to Pattaya, every baht you spend on this place gives you back quality beyond its price, in exchange for accepting that the facilities and luxury still aren't on par with the big hotels — which, for a stay in this price range, is a very worthwhile trade

Things to know before booking — a few things help make the stay smoother · one, if you're a light sleeper or sensitive to noise, ask for a high-floor room or one that doesn't face the main road right at booking, because it's an in-town industrial stay with some traffic noise · two, if you want an airy room with a balcony, specify a Deluxe Double or Deluxe Twin with balcony, because the Standard Room may not have one · three, if you're staying a week or a month, ask the property directly about the monthly rate — it's much better value than booking nightly · four, on breakfast, don't expect a big chain-hotel buffet — if you like Western dishes you may need to walk out to the cafés around · five, the pool is a small rooftop pool, better for a soak and a lounge than serious swimming, so set your expectations beforehand · six, if you come by car, free parking is a plus, but ask about the number of spaces during busy periods · seven, on long holidays and in peak season rooms fill up fast, so book ahead and compare prices across platforms, and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't firm yet

Summary — from all the real reviews, Triple B Boutique Residence is the best fit for anyone who wants a clean room, a good bed, and a central Si Racha location on a very light budget, whether you're coming to work in the eastern industrial zone, on a short stopover, staying monthly, or using it as a base for day trips to Pattaya · clean rooms that are bigger than the price, big bathrooms, balconies, a rooftop pool, a gym, free parking, 24-hour check-in, and a location within walking distance of Robinson Si Racha make it good value in quality-for-price terms — hard to find a rival in the area · if you're looking for a luxurious beachfront resort with a spa, several restaurants, a large pool, and five-star service, this isn't the answer, and you should consider a big chain hotel in Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · but for a trip where you want a clean, well-priced stay in central Si Racha with solid basics and friendly staff — Triple B genuinely answers that need well, and that's why it earns a high-8 score from a large number of real reviews

faq.q: Where is Triple B Boutique Residence · what can you get to from there?
faq.a: The property is at 233/8 Moo 2, Surasak, Si Racha, Chonburi 20110 in central Si Racha · it's a walk to Robinson Si Racha and Pacific Park, about 400 metres, near the Sriracha Shinto Shrine and Si Racha Junction railway station · close to the Laem Chabang estates and port, about 20 minutes from Pattaya, and roughly an hour from both Suvarnabhumi and U-Tapao airports

faq.q: What's the starting price at Triple B Boutique Residence · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start around ฿800/night for a Standard Room at normal rates (during some promotions it drops to roughly ฿600–700) · there are Deluxe Double and Deluxe Twin rooms with balcony, and a Deluxe Studio (double + single bed) for a small family · for long-stay guests there's a monthly rate starting around ฿7,000/month — best to ask the property directly

faq.q: Who is Triple B Boutique Residence good for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people coming to work in the eastern industrial zone, travellers who want a clean, low-cost room in town, and monthly guests staying near work · it's also handy as a base for day trips to Pattaya · if you're after a luxurious beachfront resort with a spa and full facilities, a big chain hotel in Bang Saen or Pattaya may suit you better

faq.q: What pool and facilities does Triple B Boutique Residence have?
faq.a: There's a rooftop pool with sun terrace (a small pool, better for a soak and a lounge than serious swimming), a gym, free parking, free Wi-Fi in all rooms, a 24-hour front desk and security, 24-hour check-in, daily housekeeping, a lift, and a convenience store in the building · breakfast is on offer (Thai dishes stand out, few Western options)

faq.q: What about noise and breakfast at Triple B · how should you prepare?
faq.a: It's a stay in an industrial town with some traffic noise, so if you're a light sleeper ask for a high-floor room or one that doesn't face the main road · reviews see breakfast differently — Thai dishes like rice porridge are tasty, but Western options are limited and some meals aren't served hot · if you like Western dishes, the cafés and restaurants around the hotel are an easy walk

faq.q: Is Triple B Boutique Residence still open · what's its review score?
faq.a: It's still open and operating normally · the score sits in the high 8s (around 8.6) from a large number of real reviews on Trip.com, with many reviews praising the clean rooms, comfy beds, the walk to Robinson, and the value · on platforms with a smaller sample the score may be lower because reviews about the small pool and breakfast are mixed in, so compare several sources before deciding
